sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: But he stresses that drone speed, rather than stealthiness, tends to come first for larger drones used in the war between Russia and Ukraine.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "Make it faster, not less quiet, seems to be the approach," says Tollast.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Sharrow Engineering developed twisted propellers that reduce noise For Detroit-based entrepreneur, Greg Sharrow, it was the challenge of broadcasting a classical music performance back in 2012 that set him on the path to quieter drone design.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: He needed to film a violinist from a tricky angle and a drone seemed the only solution – except that it would be far too noisy.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: As a starting point, "I knew that most of the noise from the drone was coming from the propeller, not the motor," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Specifically, it was the tips of the blades that he realised were creating the noise as they swiped through the air.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "I asked myself a very simple question, what would a tipless propeller look like and how would it function?" The result was to create a propeller with twisted loop-shaped blades with no points.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It turned out it was easier to test his propeller in water than it was to repeatedly fly a drone, which led Sharrow to initially develop a less noisy boat propeller.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: A review of the main disability benefit has recommended an overhaul of the system to allow disabled people to "achieve better health, higher living standards and greater independence".
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The report proposes both short and long terms changes to the personal independence payment (Pip) for claimants in England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The benefit is claimed by four million people and is available to people whether they are in work or unemployed.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Its aim is to help with the additional costs of being disabled.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Pip benefit system 'not fit for purpose' and 'dehumanising' assessments should change, review finds - follow live This is the first review of the benefit since it was introduced in 2013.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: More than 40,000 disabled people engaged with the process with more than 90% of them saying they'd had a negative experience while applying for Pip, describing it as stressful, dehumanising or psychologically damaging.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The review concludes the Pip process is "not fit for purpose" and calls for a fundamental redesign.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: While the review was chaired by Sir Stephen Timms, the disability minister, the experience of disabled people is clear throughout the review.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: A fast-track process should be introduced for two types of claimants.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Those with terminal illnesses should get the fastest route to an award to ensure their lives are as comfortable as possible.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Those who have severe conditions that are well-evidenced and unlikely to change over time, and whose impact on daily living is clear, should also receive the benefit without a full assessment.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Any subsequent review should avoid unnecessary reassessments.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Other claimants will have to go through an updated initial assessment.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: This will examine how a person's condition affects their daily life – functions, barriers, and needs that are currently not being met.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: This assessment will determine entitlement to the benefit.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: It will also decide the level of cash award, which will remain the bedrock of the benefit.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Optional referrals to support services should also be offered but this will be voluntary and a refusal to engage with them should not affect the benefit level.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: A new set of questions should be developed to better understand the extra costs a person faces, but will not ask them to calculate costs or provide receipts.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The system should recognise fluctuating and cumulative needs and produce decisions that are consistent and be robust against misuse.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The 28-day hospitalisation rule – which sees Pip payments suspended if someone spends more than 28 days as an inpatient – should also be reviewed as claimants find it can cause unnecessary stress and can delay discharges from hospitals.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The inquiry was not set up to find savings in the system despite the fact that spending on Pip is forecast to cost more than £40bn by 2030.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: In the year before the Covid pandemic, Pip cost £16.3bn when adjusted for inflation to today's prices.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The report acknowledges that since the benefit was introduced, the number of people receiving disability benefits has increased across every age group for both men and women.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Most of the increase has happened between 2019 and 2024, with the sharpest increases among young people aged 16-19, people in their 30s and women, whose rates of benefit receipt have risen faster than men's.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The report says that a reformed Pip system that more accurately reflects peoples' needs will likely mean "a rebalancing process".
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: While the review didn't set out to make savings, it couldn't increase the overall costs and with some people likely to gain, others will almost certainly lose some cash.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The review is not explicit on who these people might be.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Separate research last month from a think tank, the Resolution Foundation, suggested that one in six Pip recipients didn't have any additional costs associated with their conditions.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: In an interview to coincide with the review, Timms said that "if people don't have extra costs, then this is not the benefit for them".
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Alan Milburn's report - which proposed widespread changes to help get young people who are not in education, employment or training (Neet) into work across the UK - recommended that Pip be removed from people under 25 as part of a package of measures to tackle youth unemployment.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Today's review does not make the same recommendation.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: It will be up to the government to decide how they marry the two reports.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: They have said they are committed to reforming the Pip assessment process, but what that means in practice probably won't be known until the New Year when they publish their considered response.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Crime scene evidence is often not enough to identify suspects Randy Gail Sperino was last seen alive on the evening of 9 November 1993, as she was getting into a pickup truck in Granite City, Illinois.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The 34-year-old's body was found hours later in a field nearby, the victim of blunt force trauma.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The identity of her killer was a mystery.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: DNA evidence found at the crime scene was tested against standard law enforcement databases, but no matches were found.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: For three decades, investigators from the Madison County Sheriff's Office chased leads and interviewed hundreds of people as they attempted to identify the perpetrator.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The case looked like it would remain one of more than 250,000 unsolved homicides in the US.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Then, last year, detectives tried a fresh approach.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: They sent genetic evidence to Othram, a Houston-based company that uses DNA technology to help identify the perpetrators in cold and current crime cases.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The Madison County detectives had been inspired by investigative genetic genealogy techniques used to identify the Golden State Killer, Joseph James DeAngelo, back in 2018.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: In that case, an investigative team constructed a family tree to help identify the killer.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: They were able to do so thanks to DNA data that relatives had provided to commercial databases, similar to consumer ancestry platforms.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Unlike traditional forensic DNA testing, which generally relies on a direct comparison between evidence and a known person, investigative genetic genealogy can identify distant genetic relatives of an unknown individual.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Othram set about applying this technique to track down Sperino's killer.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: While the suspect's own DNA profile wasn't available, profiles submitted by his extended relatives allowed the company to identify a male family member.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: "That lead broke the case open," said Captain Tim Lawrence of Madison County Sheriff's Office, which was responsible for investigating the crime.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: It was a crucial clue that led the detectives to Albert "Buddy" Zigler, 70, who police say then confessed to the murder.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: He was charged in May this year.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Wes Sperino, Gail's son, said at a press conference: "I finally get closure and I finally know who did this." Albert Zigler was charged with murder in May The technique that led detectives to Zigler is credited with revolutionising how forensic cases are solved.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: It has been highly successful in helping solve cases involving unidentified human remains and identifying suspects in longstanding investigations.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Othram claims it has helped solve thousands of cases.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: However, Mittelman is quick to point out that DNA technology can only go so far before "a cascade of investigative steps" are needed.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: An Othram scientist prepares a bone for DNA extraction DNA science isn't the only technology that is helping detectives solve cold cases.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: One of the challenges facing detectives on major investigations like the hunt for Sperino's attacker is the sheer amount of evidence they dig up.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Officers investigating her murder realised AI could help them wade through the mountains of evidence they had accumulated since 1993.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: They used a platform called Centerline AI, from Florida software company CentralSquare, to analyse more than 2,000 pages of records and identify evidence for the DNA testing that helped to break the case.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The AI helped them reconstruct timelines and organise witness information.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: "It's so much easier than having a detective have to read through 2,000 pages," Lawrence says.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: His team could interact with the AI like a chat bot.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: This also helped when it came to interviewing Zigler after they had tracked him down.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Detectives were able to ask questions of the AI to help "figure out if Zigler was being truthful", says Lawrence.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: But the technology is "only as good as the investigator," says the captain.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: There comes a point, he says, "where you leave the technology behind and you have to go track people down and talk to them." Investigative genetic genealogy has its limitations too.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Mittelman says: "It can't solve every case.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: If you have no DNA, you can't really use this technique." "But this technique is a lot more powerful and a lot more likely to yield identities than having to rely on the chance that you find a match somewhere in a database," he adds.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: While firms like Othram only use ancestry platforms where users have provided consent for law enforcement matching, there remain some concerns about the ethical implications of using this data.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: "There are significant privacy concerns," says Denise Syndercombe Court, professor of forensic genetics at King's College London.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: While one person may have opted in to their DNA being used, genetic relatives may not have given consent.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: A lack of funding is another hurdle.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Mittelman says: "Every law enforcement agency wants to do it.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: There's just not a lot of funding for it." Sometimes cases are funded through donations or crowdfunding.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Othram operates a website listing cases that members of the public can help fund.

sentences.text: Rashdan Technologies collects and processes such human generated data.

sentences.text: "For a lot of these people, that's meaningful," Baig says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Making sure workers give their consent and are comfortable with the process is important, he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: For example: applying the correct grip force so a plastic bottle doesn't crumble versus a steel glass," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: And until recently, that data was not available.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: At the moment his firm has 96,000 data collectors across countries in Latin America and Southeast Asia.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Wandsworth prison, in south London, is among those that would be closed by the Conservatives London's Victorian jails should be closed down and the land sold off to property developers, the Conservatives have said, as they launched a plan to massively increase prison places in England and Wales.

sentences.text: Non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) signed by staff at the UK's information watchdog will be lifted to allow them to speak out about its culture, the government has confirmed.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: Ministers are expected to publish the details of how an independent review of the working environment at the Information Commission will be carried out next week.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: It follows the departure of the watchdog's boss five months ago amid allegations of sexually inappropriate behaviour.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: A government spokesperson confirmed that NDAs, known as "gagging clauses", would not be enforced by the Information Commission, saying the regulator "will not use the terms of any agreement to prevent people from participating in the review".
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: The government "will set out further details on the review, including its terms of reference and the independent reviewer, shortly", they added.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: The Information Commission is one of the UK's most high-profile regulators charged with the crucial task of regulating AI, data protection and Freedom of Information requests.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: It recently won a court battle with TikTok after it fined the social media platform £12.7m for misusing children's data, and has penalised bodies including the Ministry of Defence after an email blunder exposed the details of interpreters fleeing Afghanistan.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: But it has been without permanent leadership since Information Commissioner John Edwards resigned earlier this year .
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: It came after an independent investigation found a "case to answer" over reports of alleged inappropriate behaviour towards staff including claims of sexual harassment.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: The Information Commission said the investigation found Edwards' behaviour "fell short of the conduct expected from a public official".
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: In a resignation statement posted on his LinkedIn page in June, Edwards said he disagreed with how the investigation had been carried out but accepted his position had "become untenable".
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: Nine of those , external included a "non-derogatory clause" which legally prevents employees from making negative comments publicly.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: While this is a small proportion of the more than 1,000 staff employed by the commissioner, government advice stipulates that public bodies should only use confidentiality clauses "when necessary" and that they should "not seek to stifle or discourage staff from raising concerns".
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: Since 2025, new laws also mean they cannot be used to silence employees subjected to harassment or abuse.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: Five months later, the investigation has not begun.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: In recent weeks, the two major civil service unions, the PCS and FDA, have pushed for an external examination of the events leading up to Edwards' resignation in meetings with government officials.

sentences.text: The unions have also asked for those who signed non-disclosure agreements with the ICO to be released from them so they can contribute to the review.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: The PCS union says other concerns had previously been raised with them about Edwards, including a bullying complaint, which was investigated at the time.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: An internal staff survey, published in August and released under FOI , external points towards wider issues at the Commission, with 14% of all employees reporting they had either personally experienced bullying, harassment and discrimination.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: Multiple current and former employees have also told the BBC of experiencing or witnessing incidents of bullying or harassment.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: PCS General Secretary Fran Heathcote said the union's members at the Commission "have been failed for too long by a toxic leadership culture that has allowed bullying and harassment to persist, leaving many staff fearful of speaking out".
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: Heathcote said she welcomed the "positive engagement" the union had received in recent weeks from the Commission and officials at the Department for Culture Media and Sport (DCMS), which oversees it.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: "Instead, a leadership vacuum has compounded what went before at a rudderless organisation where it seems the worst behaviours in the workplace are not being challenged," she added.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: She said it was "vital" the government brought in "someone who can set a new tone and is dedicated to changing attitudes and protecting staff" to head up the Commission.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the Information Commission said its commitment to an independent review reflected its "ongoing commitment to listening and learning from the events of the past year and those leading up to it".

sentences.text: CT scans before (left) and after treatment with daraxonrasib plus chemotherapy (gemcitabine and nabpaclitaxel) showing multiple tumours that are no longer visible.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Yellow arrows indicate the tumours visible before treatment Experts are calling it the biggest breakthrough in pancreatic cancer treatment for decades - a daily pill that appears to shrink and possibly even eliminate tumours in some patients with one of the deadliest and hardest-to-treat cancers.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Cancer became undetectable on scans in one in 12 of the patients given daraxonrasib along with chemotherapy in early medical trials.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 participants who had recently been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: But doctors stress it is unclear how long it might keep the disease at bay and should not be seen as a cure.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Cancer Research UK called it "the biggest leap forward in decades" for pancreatic cancer patients.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: The charity's Dr Sam Godfrey told BBC News that the results were incredibly exciting.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: "What this new drug has done is it's found a way of drugging the undruggable.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: "We are finally seeing progress in pancreatic cancer which is so long overdue." Pancreatic cancer is notoriously hard to treat and has the lowest survival rate of all common cancers in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Although chemotherapy can shrink tumours a bit, the cancer often grows again.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Most patients with advanced disease survive months, not years.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Doctors hope the new treatment might offer patients more time, even if it cannot stop cancers for good.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: The trial followed patients for a year and a half, on average, and some did not see their cancer return during this time.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: "We are beginning to see not only a higher percentage of tumour response rates, but also deeper responses and a near doubling in the duration of disease control, which may eventually translate into longer survival," he said.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Daraxonrasib is a targeted inhibitor treatment that has already been approved in the US .
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: It works by locking on to and shutting off certain mutations, called RAS , external , found in most pancreatic cancers that drive tumour growth.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Dozens of other cancers, including lung and ovarian, can have similar mutations, meaning the drug might help lots of other patients too.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Dr Godfrey said: "I would hope that the early success that we are beginning to see in pancreatic cancer can also be rolled out to other cancers." He said longer trials and results were vital.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: In Britain, there are 11,500 diagnoses of the disease each year and around 10,200 deaths, according to Cancer Research UK.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Actor Alan Rickman died of the disease in 2016, five months after diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Symptoms can include , external jaundice, itchy skin, darker pee, paler poo, unexplained weight loss, tiredness and high temperature.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Early efforts to contain coronavirus "were doomed to fail" because the test, trace and isolate system in the UK could only handle a relatively small number of cases, the seventh report of the Covid inquiry says in a damning assessment.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Across 245 pages the inquiry looks at everything from border controls to how well contact tracing worked.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report said the virus was allowed to spread virtually unchecked in the first few months after community testing and contact tracing was abandoned in mid-March 2020, costing lives.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Ministers said this was because testing capacity was being overwhelmed.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: NHS Test and Trace was launched two months later and eventually became one of the biggest testing services in the world per head of population.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the end, more than £30bn was spent across the UK during the pandemic on testing, tracing and isolating.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Once established, it was effective.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: But in those early months the four UK nations were "effectively blind" to how quickly Covid was spreading, the inquiry said.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It criticises the government for not having a robust test, trace and isolate system in place to start with, saying this, alongside other failures, meant harsher measures, including lockdown and school closures, were needed.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Inquiry chair Baroness Hallett said the UK should have been better prepared and learnt lessons from other countries that had experience of dealing with outbreaks of other infectious diseases, such as Sars.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Unlike the UK, places such as Hong Kong, South Korea, Singapore and Taiwan had established systems ready to go.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: This was despite the fact the UK had run a series of simulation exercises in the years leading up to Covid.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: They included Exercise Cygnus into a flu pandemic and Exercise Alice into Mers.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Both identified problems relating to test, trace or isolation, which appear not to have been fully acted on.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report also raises the question of whether the government could have made use of non-government testing facilities in hospitals, universities and the private sector from the start, instead of just relying on 12 government labs.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: When people in the UK were told to isolate, "many felt forgotten and let down by the lack of practical or financial support when trying to follow the rules", says the report.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the early months of the pandemic, estimates suggested less than half of people were complying with the rules around isolating if infected.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Ministers and their advisers discussed this and fines of up to £10,000 were introduced for those who did not comply, which some experts have said was counter-productive.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Changes were made to allow people to claim statutory sick pay.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: But it was not until September in England – and later in Scotland and Wales – that £500 financial payments were introduced to help those on low incomes comply.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: More also needed to be done to provide practical support for things such as collecting medicines and shopping for food for those who did not have people to call on.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Suspending all flights from China to the UK in February 2020 could "have provided valuable additional time to prepare healthcare systems for the impact of the pandemic", said inquiry chair Baroness Hallett.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report says the UK lacked a clear strategy for implementing border control measures early in the pandemic, which left the country in an "extremely vulnerable position".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: By contrast, the UK government only requested travellers arriving from high-risk areas to self-isolate for 14 days.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The UK government implemented no further border control measures until June 2020.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report says that border controls were a "critical gap in the UK's ability to limit the spread of the virus" and recommends that in the future "international border control measures should be in place at the earliest stages of a pandemic".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The inquiry report is more positive about the use of smartphone apps, saying digital tools can have a "significant impact on reducing the spread of infection".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It quotes a mathematical modelling study from the US which estimates that, when 75% of people used a contact tracing app in the pandemic, infections were reduced by at least 50%.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Three different apps were developed during Covid - one for England and Wales, another for Scotland and a third for Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The inquiry says that took up "valuable time", and it recommends developing a UK-wide digital tool to use in any future outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It says it is "fundamentally important" that apps and digital tools are as accurate as possible – and people have confidence in them.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the summer of 2021, as Covid restrictions were relaxed, around 7% of all UK adults were told to self-isolate over a seven-day period, something dubbed by the press as the "pingdemic".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It quotes Treasury estimates suggesting that may have reduced economic growth by as much as 0.3% that month.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: More than 200 doctors have had their details sent in error to the Times newspaper The doctors' regulator the General Medical Council (GMC) has apologised after it mistakenly sent information about more than 220 doctors to a national newspaper.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The information included summaries of complaints alleging antisemitism or Islamophobia against the doctors.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: For some of the medics involved, it was only when the GMC alerted them to the data breach that they discovered a complaint had been made about them.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC says it is "very sorry" for the incident and has reported itself to the Information Commissioner's Office.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC - an independent body that regulates doctors, physician associates and anaesthesia associates to protect patient safety - sent the information about 223 doctors to a journalist at the Times newspaper.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: While no names were revealed, GMC identification numbers were included, which would easily allow doctors to be found on the regulator's register.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Some doctors have also raised concerns that their ethnicity was included in the data breach.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: All the medics involved have been the subject of a complaint involving either antisemitism or Islamophobia, dating from the Hamas attack on Israel in October 2023 to September 2026.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC says it has a legal and statutory responsibility to investigate such claims.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the Times is understood to have promised not to make any of the  details public, but has said it will not delete the information.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: A spokesman for the doctor's trade union, the British Medical Association (BMA), condemned the release of personal information.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "The BMA is aware that a number of doctors have received communication from the GMC to say that it erroneously sent personal identifiable data about them to the Times newspaper when responding to a media request," it said.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "The GMC must take action to ensure such a breach never occurs again." The BMA said it would look at ways to support members affected and urged them to make contact via their website.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: A doctors' campaign group, The Doctors' Association UK (DAUK), called for an independent investigation into the error.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "If a doctor sent identifiable patient information to a newspaper, they could expect to be referred to the GMC," said Dr Matt Kneale, DAUK co-chairman.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "The GMC should hold itself to the same standard of confidentiality it expects from doctors.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Just over a quarter of complaints over Islamophobia - 26% - have led to disciplinary action.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: But other complaints were closed, having failed to reach the threshold for investigation.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC said it had contacted the doctors affected to explain what had happened, to apologise and provide information and support.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: A spokesperson added: "We recognise the concern this will cause to both those impacted personally and other registrants and we are very sorry this happened.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "Our priority continues to be supporting those affected and taking steps to reduce the impact of this incident." Clarification 20 November: This article was amended on 19 November to remove references to the information being 'leaked'.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The information was mistakenly disclosed by the GMC in response to a media request.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Adverts for tests and services relating to low testosterone are allowed but must be rooted in evidence, the regulator said Five adverts by online healthcare provider Voy have been banned by the watchdog for making misleading claims linked to low testosterone in men.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) said the adverts promoted Voy's at-home testosterone blood tests in three posters and two paid-for Facebook ads.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: It said they were misleading as they linked common symptoms such as irritability and fatigue to low testosterone.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: Voy said it had withdrawn the adverts while the investigation was under way and would not run them again.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: The NHS says that while testosterone levels in men fall as they age, this is "unlikely" to cause any problems in itself.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: It adds , external that while a testosterone deficiency in later life can sometimes be responsible for symptoms such as depression, loss of sex drive, erectile dysfunction, and other physical and emotional symptoms, they are often not linked.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: Voy is a company that sells products such as testosterone, menopause and weight loss treatments.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: Some of its testosterone test kit adverts drew a backlash online earlier this year when they appeared on the London Underground.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: Some described them as "ragebait" for using phrases such as "It's not him, it's his hormones" and "Men get hormonal too".
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: At the time Voy said it was trying to destigmatise conversations about men's health.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: Some of the adverts sparked discussion online after appearing at Tube stations The ASA's ruling, however, took issue with how some of the adverts "exaggerated the connection between several common symptoms, which can have many possible causes, and low testosterone".
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: The ASA gave examples such as low sex drive, low energy, loss of motivation and changes in mood.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: "While some symptoms may be more closely associated with the condition, others were much less specific and shouldn't have been presented as strong indicators of low testosterone in isolation," the watchdog said.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: It added that one of the Facebook adverts also included the claim that "low testosterone sneaks up on 1 in 4 men over 30".
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: The ASA said this was misleading and not supported by the evidence provided by Voy.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: Dr Earim Chaudry, chief medical officer for Voy, said: "Every patient decision at Voy is clinician-led and these campaigns were developed to align with UK advertising standards.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: We keep all our advertising under continual review to ensure it meets any updated guidance." Wednesday's ruling followed two others in August by the watchdog, which found misleading claims in adverts for testosterone testing services from online providers BioID Health and Numan Digital Healthcare.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: The rulings form part of a wider ASA investigation into adverts aimed at men concerned about their health.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: This has identified a "recurring theme of advertisers playing on insecurities around libido, erectile problems, testosterone and ageing", the regulator said.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: The watchdog said adverts for tests and services relating to low testosterone were allowed, but businesses needed to make sure the claims they made were accurate and supported by evidence.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: Baroness Cass said the current wording of the bill risked "serious unintended consequences" The author of the independent review into gender identity services for young people says she does not support the current draft bill banning conversion practices - having previously welcomed it.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: Baroness Cass told BBC Radio 4's Today programme while it is "desirable" to ban the practices, "the challenge is that we have not yet as far as I can see got a workable bill".
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: At a parliamentary committee scrutinising the bill, she also said it risked "serious unintended consequences" for parents of children suffering gender distress, or medical professionals working in that area.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: A government spokesperson said they welcomed her comments.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: They added they would take all evidence put forward by the committee seriously as they "want to get this ban right".
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: The government has said the bill would protect LGBT people in England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: Conversion practices are generally described as interventions, treatments or activities designed to change or suppress someone's sexual orientation or gender identity.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: This can sometimes happen in religious or family settings and can be very distressing for the person at the centre of it.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: There have been long-running campaigns in the UK to outlaw such practices, and in its 2024 manifesto, the Labour party promised to introduce a bill banning them.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: When the government introduced its draft legislation , external in June this year, Baroness Cass was quoted in the publicity for it , external .
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: But asked at the Draft Conversion Practices Bill committee if she supported the bill's current form, she said simply "no".
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: Baroness Cass said the increased "polarisation" used in the debate around gender meant people may use the new law in a way that wasn't intended.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: The current wording of the bill requires the victim to suffer "serious harm to the individual's physical or mental health, or serious alarm or distress to the individual which has a substantial adverse effect on their usual day-to-day activities".
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: But Baroness Cass said she worried this wording left open the possibility of "vexatious" complaints that could put therapists working with young gender-distressed people at risk of prosecution.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: "Therapeutic interactions can be distressing and often are because you're discussing quite sensitive issues," she told the Today programme.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: "The problem is the chilling effect of professionals knowing that they may be open to complaint, and indeed prosecution," she told the Today programme.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: Baroness Cass also raised concerns about the possible impact the new law could have on families.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: She said that, for instance, if a parent stopped a child's money if they thought they might buy a "breast binder or hormones" that this may also fall within the scope of the bill and result in prosecution.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: Asked about her apparent support for the bill when it was first published, Baroness Cass said that she was in favour of the idea but had not had the time to read the details before the press release was to be published, but went ahead and gave the quote anyway.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: When she published her report on gender identity services for young people in 2024, she described conversion practices as "abhorrent".
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: She says she still feels no LGBT people should be subjected to conversion practices.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: She told the committee she wants "a bill that protects the people it's supposed to protect, but doesn't accidentally entrap those who you don't want to [entrap]".
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: The bill has received support from several LGBT charities, such as Stonewall, and organisations like the British Association for Counselling and Psychotherapy.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: The government said: "We want to get this ban right, which is why we have put this draft bill forward for pre-legislative scrutiny.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: "We welcome both Baroness Cass's support for taking action to end abusive conversion practices, and her comments on the need for legislation to avoid adverse consequences.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: "We will take all evidence put forward by the committee seriously as we move forward in ending almost a decade of delay for LGBT+ people who should never have to suffer abuse in an effort to change who they are." The committee hearings continue.
sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.text: From Spring 2027, under 16s will no longer be able to access several social media applications More than 300,000 young people in Britain will work with researchers to help understand how the UK's forthcoming social media ban for under-16s could affect mental health.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: The studies will examine the habits of the children and teenagers, including whether they spend less time on their phones and what they are replacing scrolling with.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Ten different projects have been commissioned, taking place across England, Wales and Scotland, to help reflect a diverse range of teenagers.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: The social media ban, beginning in spring 2027, will follow a similar model to that already introduced in Australia to stop children accessing platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Apps such as Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, Snapchat and YouTube will be banned under new rules The work, funded by health charity The Wellcome Trust, will help inform future online safety policies in the UK and internationally, with some early results available before the ban happens.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Researchers will use wearable technology, smartphones, digital diaries and surveys to collect data to see how young people respond to the ban, both physically and mentally.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: And they will check whether young people find ways to circumvent restrictions.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Dr Camilla Iannone, research lead at Wellcome, said it was a once-in-a-generation opportunity to study at scale how social media and its restrictions affected youth mental health.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: The best way to stop the disease spreading is to give antibiotics to people who may have come into contact with it.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Vaccination can also provide some protection from future infection.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Anyone becoming unwell with symptoms of meningitis or sepsis should seek medical help urgently at the closest Accident and Emergency Department or by dialling 999.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Early treatment can be lifesaving.

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England
