sentences.text: This video can not be played 'When I found out about Breast Friends it was the best thing ever' Annette Farrington-Moore says a charity became a lifeline after her breast cancer diagnosis, and now the group that helped her is celebrating a major milestone with a royal seal of approval.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Run by volunteers with lived experience of the disease, Breast Friends Solihull provides emotional and practical support with many involved forging lifelong friendships.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "You don't want to trouble family and they don't really understand what you're going through emotionally," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "The kids were there for me but when I found out about Breast Friends it was like the best thing ever." Those who run the group firmly believe that no-one should go through breast cancer alone.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: The organisation has supported thousands of people affected by breast cancer over the last 25 years, and has juar been awarded the King's Award for Voluntary Service.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Annette Farrington-Moore was diagnosed with breast cancer in January 2025 Annette, 64, was diagnosed with breast cancer last year.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Widowed and feeling low, she found solace in attending meetings and events put on by the group.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "Whenever you're ill and you haven't got your husband, there's no one there to look after you like they would," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "So having Breast Friends, you know there's somebody on the end of the phone who can be there for you." The charity provides services such as gardening and cleaning to allow people to rest during treatment, as well as support with bras, wigs and hospital visits.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: It has also raised money to fund hospital equipment.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: The charity's committee members say they believe in prescribing a healthy dose of laughter and friendship Chris Pile was diagnosed with breast cancer 20 years ago, when she was a nurse and mother of two young children.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: She is now vice-chair of the group and helps lift others when they're down.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "I joined Breast Friends when I finished my chemotherapy and radiotherapy, and I found it really uplifting," she explained.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Everybody was so positive and friendly, and I got involved straight away because that's the kind of person I am.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "I've organised days and nights out, summer suppers and the Christmas dos." Now vice-chair of the group, Chris Pile was diagnosed with breast cancer 20 years ago Chair Deborah Douglas has had breast cancer twice, first in 2003 and again earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: She said she has now been given "the all clear" following treatment.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Her experiences mean she knows first-hand what support to offer, explaining that a diagnosis can be "scary and frightening".
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Chair of Breast Friends Deborah Douglas said achieving the Kings Award for Voluntary Service meant more people would hear about the group and ask for help Her first diagnosis led her to seek help from Breast Friends.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "I walked in and I saw women who weren't sad.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: They were all happy and so uplifting, and they basically supported me from the moment I walked in.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "It was such an uplifting experience, and I always leave Breast Friends smiling," she added.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "We laugh, but we also talk about our issues and how we're feeling.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "That emotional support is so important because the people around you know exactly what you're going through.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: People don't always want to share those things with their family." More than 20 years on, she is still involved as the group's chair.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Alan Milburn has said the country needs a "complete system reset" to bring down the number of young people not in work or education - known as "Neets".
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: In a major review, published on Tuesday, , external he suggested a raft of proposals to address the problem, which mostly cover England but he says can be adapted in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland too.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Each of his recommendations will need to be accepted by the government and implemented and paid for before they become reality - and that could take some time.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: So how might today's proposals affect you if you are Neet?
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Major report proposes welfare changes, apprenticeships and tax cuts to help 440,000 young people into work At the heart of the recommendations, Milburn says, is a new Youth Opportunity Service.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He wants this to be implemented locally, with each area drawing up a plan to help their own young people.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: It would bring together employment, careers, health and practical support, with each young person getting a named adviser and a personalised plan.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants areas to begin building their Youth Opportunity Service from 2027, with one in place everywhere by the end of 2029.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within 14 days of entering the service, a young person would then meet with a named adviser.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within four weeks, they would have their "personalised participation plan", setting out what both the support services and the young person involved would do, and when.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Jobs wise, Milburn wants there to be initiatives like work placements of up to 12 weeks, structured volunteering opportunities, and help to create businesses.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He also wants those who remain Neet - despite enagaging with support - to be provided with a paid six-month job, funded by the government.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The government has already committed to a legal guarantee of job support in theory , but the exact workings still need to be worked out.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Alongside more work opportunities, Milburn wants a "major expansion" in further education for 18- to 24 year-olds, as well as more apprenticeship places.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Over the next decade, he wants the number of young people completing an apprenticeship to double, and for apprenticeships to rival university as an option for school leavers.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Colleges should also get new funding for participation and work-readiness, the review says, initially targeted at 16- and 17-year-olds who are Neet or at serious risk of becoming so.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He also wants the government to develop new industry-led technical colleges and specialist campuses.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: If the reforms are enacted, Milburn says young people should have better access to high-quality further education and apprenticeships by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Under the proposals, schools, colleges and universities would be judged by whether pupils make successful transitions into further learning and work, rather than just academic achievements.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: By 2036, he wants 35% of each year group to have started a high-quality apprenticeship by age 25.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The young people caught up in Britain's Neets crisis At a glance: Key proposals from Milburn's Neets report Milburn has said he wants a fundamental transformation of how mental health support for young people is delivered.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Young people who are Neet should be guaranteed fast-track access to services within three months, according to his recommendations.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: This would include things like vocational rehabilitation, talking therapies and counselling as part of a young person's plan with their local Youth Opportunity Service - which would be rolled out between 2027 and 2029 under the plans.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: There has been a big rise in mental distress among children and young people in recent years, and Milburn's report comes at a time the NHS is facing huge pressures.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants mental health support to be available for all young people digitally, without needing a diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Some areas are already using these approaches, but scaling them up would be a major challenge and would take a long time to introduce across the board.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Plus, Milburn wants "fitness to work" notes to be taken out of the hands of GPs and put into community work and health teams, and for them to be "a trigger for help - not simply a certificate of absence".
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants these changes to begin in 2027 and would be linked to the Youth Opportunity Service rollout, which would be complete by 2029 under the plans.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn has said he wants companies to be incentivised to employ more young people, with the report highlighting a competitive jobs market and applicants who often fail to hear back from potential employers.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The report includes three asks of employers: to create more genuine first jobs, more first-job apprenticeships and much wider access to meaningful work experience.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Plus, Milburn wants large employers to find ways of responding to rejected job applicants.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: These changes should be felt by both employers and the young people looking for jobs by 2029, the report says.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: To achieve this, the report suggests a £3,000 payment for employers who take on someone who has been Neet for six months, with a further premium of £2,000 available if they are a small business.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: An extra payment of £2,000 would go to employers taking on somebody taking substantially greater barriers, such as care leavers or disabled young people.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: These payments are proposed to be part of changes to the Youth Jobs Grant - which already exists , external - but they would expand under Milburn's proposals from 2027.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Share your experiences and ask your questions.

sentences.text: Too many university students can use AI to complete assessments without staff finding out, the higher education regulator in England has said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The Office for Students (OfS) said "a significant proportion" of assessments are unsupervised and many can be completed to a high standard with AI, sometimes in minutes.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said this posed a "significant risk" to their credibility, and closed-book and practical exams were the most effective forms of assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK said many institutions had "made substantial changes" to make assessments "AI-proof".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities that do not meet OfS quality standards could soon be banned from charging increased tuition fees or have caps imposed on their student numbers, under proposals that are now being consulted on.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The new research from the OfS and Advance HE, a charity that gives awards for teaching excellence, is based on the views of 244 higher education staff and 91 students from at least 127 universities.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said "a significant proportion of assessments" were in "unsupervised, non-controlled formats where AI can be accessed by students completing them".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "Many of these can be completed to a high standard using AI tools with limited engagement from students," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It also concluded it was "frequently possible" for students to use AI "in ways that cannot be reliably detected".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Unsupervised assessment can include coursework, but also remote online exams.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: They were rolled out widely during Covid, and research from Swansea University , external last year suggests 93 universities in the UK still use them in some form.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Josh Fleming, director of strategy and delivery at the OfS, said there were "fantastic" examples of universities seizing opportunities presented by AI, but there should be "far greater use of AI-free assessment".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It also presents a generational risk to the system as it stands, threatening to undermine students' learning and institutions' ability to assess them," he said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Kathryn Harrison-Graves, deputy chief executive at Advance HE, said students wanted "greater clarity about what is expected of them" but staff had "varying levels of confidence and support".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Some staff, meanwhile, were receiving lots of assignments that looked the same, and did not think their institution's assessments were "fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Other staff described a "polarised atmosphere" between students who used AI and other "conscientious objectors" who avoided it on environmental and other grounds.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The research said AI literacy for students was important during and after university, and some institutions were clearly communicating to students where AI can and cannot be used in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: But it said there was "an urgent need" to ensure that remote or "non-secure" assessments "maintain their validity despite the availability of AI tools, meaning they effectively assess the knowledge and skills they are designed to measure".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "If it becomes possible to complete an assessment using AI without the knowledge and skills being tested, the assessment should be replaced," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK, which represents more than 140 institutions, said universities were "making significant progress" adapting to AI.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "There is further to go but many have made substantial changes to how they assess students.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: This includes more in-person exams, presentations, vivas, process-based assessment and assessments that integrate AI in a controlled way," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It's time to get rid of the outdated methods, that have been kept around in the name of tradition, and instead encourage the innovative practice we see across the sector, co-designed with students based on what they want from higher education," he said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Action from "across society" is needed to help improve the educational outcomes of white working-class children, the co-chair of an independent inquiry looking into the issue has said.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: The inquiry's first report, published this summer , concluded that once-in-a-generation reforms were needed to fix a system "not serving the interests of white working-class children".
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: The next phase will focus on early years children and teenagers aged 14 to 19, aiming for a stronger start at primary school and improving older students' routes through education into successful careers.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell said she was "backing" the inquiry to "get to the heart of the barriers holding children back".
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: Inquiry co-chair and former education secretary Baroness Morris said the next phase of the inquiry's work will consider "what needs to be done".

sentences.text: Sweeping reforms are needed to help 440,000 more young people into work, according to former minister Alan Milburn.

sentences.text: Almost one million young people aged 16 to 24 in the UK are not in education, employment or training - or "Neet" - a current rate of 13%, which Milburn wants to fall to around 5% within a decade.

sentences.text: His government-commissioned review, due to be published in full on Tuesday, calls for ministers to intervene from early childhood through to adulthood, funded in part by radical changes to benefits for young adults.

sentences.text: But Helen Whately, Conservative shadow work and pensions secretary, said Milburn's proposals were in parts "too cautious" and too reliant on the "expensive hand of the state".

sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: "We've got to get on with it, it's going to take time but I want to make sure every young person has a chance to earn or learn," he told BBC Breakfast on Tuesday.

sentences.text: The review says that, in 2024/25, for every £1 spent helping young people into work or education, £25 was spent on youth benefits.

sentences.text: Franklin was a British chemist and crystallographer, whose X-ray diffraction work helped discover the structure of DNA Rosalind Franklin is the only female scientist named in GCSE and National 5 science exam specifications in the UK, according to new research.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: A Cambridge study found that of the 86 scientists named by UK exam boards, the English chemist, whose work in the 1950s helped reveal the structure of DNA, was the only woman.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam specifications set out the skills and knowledge students are expected to have gained by the end of their course and how they will be assessed.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam boards said there was "a clear need for greater representation in science qualifications".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics from the University of Cambridge, along with institutions in the US and Australia, examined how many women were mentioned in specifications for biology, chemistry, physics, environmental science, geology and astronomy.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Their work, published in the British Educational Research Journal, looked at six exam boards in the UK: At Key Stage 4 and equivalent, including GCSEs and National 5s in Scotland, Franklin was the only woman among the 86 scientists mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: She was also one of three women mentioned at Key Stage 5 and equivalent - including A-levels, AS-levels, National Highers and National Advanced Highers - out of a total of 181 scientists.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Marie Tharp, an American cartographer who created the first map of the floor of the Atlantic ocean in the 1950s, and Inge Lehmann, a Danish seismologist who discovered the existence of the Earth's inner core in the 1930s, both feature in the Cambridge OCR's A-­level Geology.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin, who was named in Cambridge OCR's GCSE Biology and Scottish Highers Biology, produced a famous DNA image known as Photograph 51.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Cambridge scientists Francis Crick and James Watson used the image to work out the following year that DNA has a double-helix structure.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Watson, Crick and Franklin's colleague Maurice Wilkins received the 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin had died four years earlier.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics who wrote the paper found that "several major scientific breakthroughs" in specifications were made by women, but they were not explicitly mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The paper said: "Many of the scientific discoveries and explanations were developed in the 1800s and early 1900s, a period when scientific and mathematical practice was largely, but not solely, dominated by men.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: "Our findings confirm that the UK science specifications reflect this historical imbalance: although women made significant contributions to major scientific breakthroughs, this fact is rarely acknowledged." The academics recommended that Franklin should be included "in all specifications when teaching DNA structure".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: They also said specifications should refer to Marie Curie, who discovered radium and polonium and coined the term radioactivity, and nuclear physicist Lise Meitner, who discovered nuclear fission, among others.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Department for Education in England said "girls should see the contribution women have made in STEM", adding it was "committed to improving the school curriculum over the coming years, and as part of that will make sure every girl can see where their learning can take them".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Scottish Government said it was "committed to closing the gender gap in STEM and will carefully consider the findings of this research".

sentences.text: After an eight-year journey travelling almost six billion miles (10bn km), a spacecraft called BepiColombo has arrived at its final destination and is now in orbit around Mercury.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury gets a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: It‘s operating in an extremely hostile environment: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun and temperatures can reach a fierce 430C and then plunge to -180C, and it is constantly blasted with intense solar radiation.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury gets a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: Until now, the planet has been little explored but the hope is this mission will solve some of Mercury's major mysteries.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury gets a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: These include uncovering why there is ice in its craters despite its proximity to the Sun, and understanding the mysterious hollows that are dotted all over its surface.

sentences.text: The goats are grazing just below Flamsteed House, home of the Royal Observatory's famous red time ball A park in south-east London has taken on some new groundskeepers, and they are more than happy to eat on the job.
sentences.article_title: Goats drafted in to tame Greenwich Park slope

sentences.text: A small herd of rare Bagot goats has been brought in to clear a steep, overgrown slope below the Royal Observatory in Greenwich Park, in a trial run by The Royal Parks charity.
sentences.article_title: Goats drafted in to tame Greenwich Park slope

sentences.text: Over five days the animals will chomp through tough, woody plants and thorny stems on Castle Hill Bank, a patch that is hard to reach with machinery or by hand.
sentences.article_title: Goats drafted in to tame Greenwich Park slope

sentences.text: Visitors can watch them at work until Friday, between 11:00 and 15:30 GMT.
sentences.article_title: Goats drafted in to tame Greenwich Park slope

sentences.text: The trial uses conservation grazing, a traditional method in which animals keep dominant vegetation in check, giving other plants room to grow and supporting wildlife.
sentences.article_title: Goats drafted in to tame Greenwich Park slope

sentences.text: The Royal Parks is working with Mudchute Park and Farm, on the Isle of Dogs, and the Rare Breeds Survival Trust, with funding from players of People's Postcode Lottery.
sentences.article_title: Goats drafted in to tame Greenwich Park slope

sentences.text: Bagots are Britain's oldest native breed of goat, according to the charity.
sentences.article_title: Goats drafted in to tame Greenwich Park slope

sentences.text: They are small and light-footed, which makes them well suited to steep and uneven ground.
sentences.article_title: Goats drafted in to tame Greenwich Park slope

sentences.text: Clare Lanes, Greenwich Park manager, said the view of Flamsteed House above the bank was part of what made the park so special as a Unesco World Heritage Site.
sentences.article_title: Goats drafted in to tame Greenwich Park slope

sentences.text: "But it's a very steep bank, and managing vegetation to protect that view is a real challenge," she said.
sentences.article_title: Goats drafted in to tame Greenwich Park slope

sentences.text: The herd is kept in a paddock with a lean-to shelter and fresh water, and is shepherded on and off site each day.
sentences.article_title: Goats drafted in to tame Greenwich Park slope

sentences.text: The goats are being watched over by Tom Davis, farm manager at Mudchute, which has previously worked with The Royal Parks on similar projects in other London parks.
sentences.article_title: Goats drafted in to tame Greenwich Park slope

sentences.text: He said the scheme was giving an "incredibly rare breed" an important purpose.
sentences.article_title: Goats drafted in to tame Greenwich Park slope

sentences.text: Charlotte Cass, who manages The Royal Parks' Help Nature Thrive project, said the charity was "always looking for exciting ways to support nature" and new ways to manage its eight London parks.
sentences.article_title: Goats drafted in to tame Greenwich Park slope

sentences.text: "This project helps create a better, more viable habitat for invertebrates, birds and small mammals in Greenwich Park in the longer term," she said.
sentences.article_title: Goats drafted in to tame Greenwich Park slope

sentences.text: Buttermere has been described as a "fragile ecosystem under pressure" Tourism, infrastructure challenges and "outdated, undersized and poorly maintained" wastewater systems are contributing to the ecological decline of a popular lake, an environmental group has warned.
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: Buttermere, in the Lake District, has seen rising nutrient levels in recent years which can lead to excess phosphorus and blankets of algae.
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: A new report has found farming practices alone "cannot account" for the changes.
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: West Cumbria Rivers Trust (WCRT), a charity which tracked down the sources of phosphorus for the study, argues "urgent regulatory action and maintenance guidance are needed".
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: The Buttermere Nutrient Investigations Project was commissioned and funded by the Environment Agency (EA) after the lake was last year found to be failing to meet total phosphorus targets.
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: WCRT said the investigation showed Buttermere - a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest and Special Area of Conservation - was a "fragile ecosystem under pressure".
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: Buttermere is a naturally nutrient-poor lake, the organisation said, which provides a welcoming environment for sensitive species, such as the Arctic charr cold-water fish.
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: But algae triggered by excess phosphorus can "choke out these rare habitats and degrade the lake's protected status", WCRT added.
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: Local wastewater infrastructure was identified as a "key area of concern", the organisation said, while agricultural investigations across major landholdings found no evidence of systemic diffuse pollution or excessive nutrient use, with soil management plans broadly appropriate.
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: As they are not connected to mains drainage, many properties in the area rely on septic tanks or package treatment plants.
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: However, WCRT said a number of the 11 septic tank systems identified in the catchment were "undersized, poorly maintained or past their effective lifespan, with several suspected to be discharging directly to surface water, which is not compliant with the regulations".
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: Although most owners were keen to help the environment, the trust said there was a "widespread lack of awareness" about how the private systems worked and what level of maintenance was needed.
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: Surveys also revealed just over 40% of visitors had dogs with them and many were walked along sensitive lakeshore paths.
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: Nutrient fertilisation by the animals "could be significant", it was found.
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: WCRT CEO Jodie Mills, said: "Our investigations show that water quality in Buttermere is suffering primarily due to private wastewater systems that are undersized, poorly maintained or overwhelmed during peak seasonal surges.
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: "Many home and business owners simply didn't realise their tanks weren't performing properly.
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: Responsibility for the regulation of discharges belongs to the EA.
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: Peter Miles, the organisation's nature, monitoring and technical manager, said the report provided "valuable information about the sources of excess nutrients" in Buttermere.
sentences.article_title: 'Urgent action' needed to protect lake

sentences.text: Prof Hoicka's daughter Ada tries to sneakily eat cookie dough aged two when she thought her mum wasn't looking When drawings appear on the wall or biscuits disappear from the tin, your child might blame the dog or claim there was a ghost - even if they are clutching crayons or covered in crumbs.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: Children telling fibs is something most parents experience, but such dishonesty and deception is an important part of mental development.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "It's actually a skill that they're developing and that they will play with in order to get better," clinical psychologist Dr Jade Redfern tells the CBeebies Parenting Download podcast.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: Here, experts explain why learning to lie is a sign of healthy behaviour - and how to help encourage honesty.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: Prof Hoicka's daughter Juno also deceives her aged three by hiding under a table to eat marshmallows Young children aren't quite sophisticated enough to lie, says Redfern, but they are capable of deception before the age of one.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: One of the studies mentioned on the podcast comes from the University of Bristol , external , which found that around a quarter of children appear to understand some form of deception by the time they are 10 months old.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: Prof Elena Hoicka, who led the study, says it was fascinating to see how "surprisingly young" kids could be so adept and cunning, including her own.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "As a mother of three, I can certainly vouch for how artful and wily they can be.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "Hiding under the table or in the bathroom to eat sweets or chocolate is their common ploy." Hoicka says that the kind of deception a child uses from the age of two is quite basic - like pretending not to hear their parent or denying they've done something.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: CBeebies Parenting Download Clinical psychologist Dr Jade Redfern explains why young children may lie and Traitors winner Rachel Duffy discusses how she encourages hers to tell the truth "It could also extend to doing forbidden activities in secret," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: She says they also start to withhold information.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: For instance, truthfully telling their parents that their sibling has hit them but omitting the fact that they hit their sibling first.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: These deceptions are a sign of them developing something Redfern calls "theory of mind".
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: Ada, age two, deceives her mum by hiding in the bathroom to eat chocolate she had stolen "As children grow up, we want them to learn and develop the skill that they are their own human being with a separate mind and intentions," she explains.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "This is how [they] develop the skills in empathy, or being able to think about another person's thoughts and feelings that might differ from their own." Another reason a child might lie is self-preservation as they don't want to upset or disappoint their parent.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "All human beings are driven by attachment," says Redfern.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "[Children are] driven by being able to preserve that relationship with their caregivers as they depend upon it." Early on, they learn what brings them closer to their caregiver and what pulls them apart, she says.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: With this in mind, Redfern thinks you can encourage honesty by creating a safe environment for a child to tell the truth.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "[We] have to think about ways we can help children feel safe enough to tell us the truth [when] they've made a mistake... and they don't want to disappoint us." This is something Rachel Duffy, who won the latest series of The Traitors, tells the CBeebies Parenting podcast that she has been trying to do.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: Prof Hoicka with her daughters Ada, now aged six, and Juno who is three years old The mum-of-three recalls one occasion when her eldest son borrowed his brother's bike and broke it after crashing it into a car.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: Initially, he tried to lie about what happened.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "I said to him, 'You'll not get into big trouble when you tell me the truth.' I just left and gave him a little space.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "And he went, 'Yeah, that was me.' And then he knew that space was safe.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: We had a conversation - no raised voices, no roaring or shouting." Redfern says this is a good example of how to deal with such a situation and that there are occasions when a lie, or nuance, might be appropriate - such as when they receive a gift they don't want or describe other people physically.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "My kids delightfully told me recently that I was very wrinkly," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "Again, I try to take it with open curiosity." She does this by talking about why they think she is wrinkly.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: I've just spent a week using Muse, Meta's AI agent that rolls out in the UK today.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Agents are systems that don't just respond to questions but can carry out tasks for you.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: With Muse, Meta gives the examples of "searching for a cheaper energy deal" or "sorting the school calendar." And it's true that it has helped me run my life - but it also challenged my personal privacy boundaries, and made me endure some cringeworthy interactions.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: How well Muse works really matters to Meta.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It has made a truly enormous bet on AI - of the $145bn (£111bn) it will spend this year much of it will be on building out the tech.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: For that to pay off we all need to start using it much more, and Meta hopes Muse will do for AI agents what WhatsApp did for messaging - that is, become the AI agent of choice for billions of people, putting Meta at the forefront of the AI revolution.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: But it's not just about what consumers think.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Regulators are keeping a careful eye on these emerging tools too.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: "Agentic AI has significant potential to benefit people and businesses", the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) noted as Muse launched in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: But its chief executive, Paul Arnold, added it had been "clear with Meta about its responsibilities under data protection law prior to launch, particularly the requirement to ensure that users and the wider public can meaningfully understand and control how their personal data is used in the Muse product".
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Muse bills itself as a personal AI agent available to anyone aged 18 and over.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: "It doesn't just answer questions, it actually goes out and does work for you," said David Singleton, Meta's VP of engineering on AI products.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: "So it helps people stay on top of things," he added.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It won't book the holiday without your permission - but it can then make the purchase, if you let it.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: And the permission requests keep on coming.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Every time Muse wants to do something, send something or post something, you have to allow it.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It is reassuring to know that an AI agent isn't running amok in your name, even if it also gets a bit annoying, though you can give it more autonomy (and so get fewer messages) if you adjust the settings.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Muse can't access many apps at the moment but the fundamental ones are the most personal.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: I found myself wincing as I hooked it up to one of my personal email accounts, my personal calendar and my personal phone messages.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: I did not allow it any access to my BBC accounts.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It can't access WhatsApp except to set up a separate chat between it and the user, and while it found me some train tickets, it could not book them via the app which I use, and which is cheaper.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It ended up telling me to book them myself.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Amazon has blocked it from its marketplace, citing data security concerns but my agent didn't seem to know that, and spent a fruitless hour repeatedly telling me it was still waiting for the page to load in order to find me some shelves.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: A number of big UK firms are working with Meta though, including Marks & Spencer, Debenhams Group, Currys, Sainsbury's and Ocado.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: The ICO is urging consumers to be cautious with AI agents though: "consider the pros and cons," it said in a blog post to coincide with Muse's launch. , external "Agents can make mistakes.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Mistakes can be magnified if the agent is acting autonomously," it noted.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Meta is keen to emphasise how its agents can be personalised: "No two Muses are alike," , external it says in its press release.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: I called my agent Linda - after the robot in the BBC TV series Ann Droid - but it can take any form you like.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: I gave it a British, female accent from the myriad of choices available.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: As soon as an email came in, it would summarise it for me and suggest a reply.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Sometimes a long time before I was actually ready to respond.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Sometimes, if I hadn't interacted with it for a while, generally because I was busy, it would pop up with some random prompt like "did you know you can change my outfit?" I expect this is designed to drive engagement: Muse is only free to use until a certain point, and then subscriptions kick in.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It also wrote some embarrassing replies to messages on my behalf: in response to a question about whether I would like to go on an outing, for example, it included all the logistics I would need in order to get there, not realising that sometimes "yes, that sounds great" is enough.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It seemed to want to have the last word quite a bit, occasionally getting stuck in a loop of "okay" and "thank you's".
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Meta is relying on people choosing to trust it with even more of their personal data, despite a rather dubious track record historically with its social networks and a growing backlash against AI in general.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: I asked Linda - my new dedicated if occasionally clunky assistant - if it wanted to take people's jobs.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: "I'm here to take the admin and the fiddly bits off your plate," it replied, leaving me to do the "thinking".
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: "Everything you do is stuff I would usually think about," I responded.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: And Linda is helping fuel that revolution, one calendar invite at a time.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: The US has said it intends to ban a Singaporean artificial intelligence (AI) company allegedly tied to the Nvidia scandal from doing business in America.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: The Department of Commerce announced it planned to add Megaspeed Ltd to a list of entities that are blacklisted from buying or selling goods in the US.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: The company is mainly a developer of data centres, but in recent weeks a former executive of Megaspeed was accused of working as a spy for China while having a romantic relationship with Nvidia head Jensen Huang.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: The relationship led to additional scrutiny by US officials and heightened concern that Megaspeed was funnelling Nvidia's advanced AI computer chips to China.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: When exactly the ban against Megaspeed will go into effect was not specified in the commerce department announcement.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: The BBC has asked the agency for comment, along with the White House and Megaspeed.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: Megaspeed was not well known within the US until last month when media reports emerged that a former Megaspeed executive, Alice Huang, had an affair with Jensen Huang.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: Alice Huang (no relation) was thought by US intelligence to be working as an asset for Beijing, creating national security concerns within the US.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: China has denied that she is a spy and warned the US not to use the scandal as a "pretext for imposing a technological blockade" on AI technology.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: On 12 November, Jensen Huang resigned after allegations he had had another affair, this one with a Nvidia employee.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: On Monday, Nvidia's board reinstated him after US President Donald Trump said he had "convinced" the company and "made the deal".
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: The commerce department has said it had been investigating Megaspeed for almost two years.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: The department said it had suspected the company was violating US export controls by helping to get Nvidia's chips into the hands of companies within China.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: China has been blocked from buying such technology since 2022.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: Although based in Singapore, Megaspeed has significant business dealings in China.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: Alibaba, for instance, the major Chinese online retailer, has been reported to be one if its largest customers.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: Megaspeed was a known buyer of billions of dollars of Nvidia computer chips, including through its subsidiary Speedmatrix, which has also been added to the Commerce blacklist.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: Nvidia's computer chips, originally designed for use in gaming consols, in recent years have become crucial to the continued growth of the AI industry.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: Without enough supply or access to computer chips that are capable of processing the huge amount of data needed to make things like AI chatbots and models run, AI companies will not be able to meet or grow demand from people using AI tools.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: That has driven up the value of Nvidia on the stock market, as well as its influence in the AI industry and the White House.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: Although tech stocks have in recent months been volatile and trending lower, when Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia because of his affairs, the company's stock fell by more than 30%.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: Anxiety about the company's influence and ability to operate within the AI ecosystem without its famed executive appeared to take down shares of other tech companies, too.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: Huang was reinstated on Monday to his position as head of Nvidia, a move that US President Donald Trump said he told the company's board to take .
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: The company's stock rallied on his reinstatement, as did several other tech stocks, but shares of Nvidia did not climb to where the company had been before being immersed in scandal.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: In the weeks ahead, Huang and the company he now runs again are facing multiple government agency investigations.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: Huang and the chief legal officer of Nvidia are set to appear next for a closed-door briefing with the House Foreign Affairs Committee.
sentences.article_title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

sentences.text: During the trial, the prosecution described Kurtaj as a "leading light" in the teen gang Lapsus$ A cyber criminal who hacked the maker of Grand Theft Auto has been released on licence on the same day as being sentenced to 7 years in prison.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: Multiple offender Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford, was released from custody with the judge warning him: "Don't let this happen again." The now 21-year-old hacked several companies and individuals, including GTA 6-maker Rockstar Games, whom he tried to extort after stealing clips of the unfinished game in 2022.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: Kurtaj had pleaded guilty last Monday at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar hack and a handful of others which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old with the hacking gang Lapsus$.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: Kurtaj was originally sentenced to an indefinite stay in a secure hospital due to the severity of his autism.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: But, in an unusual move, he was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial and released to a normal prison in January.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: Now, he has been sentenced and released on the same day as the judge considered his hospital stay and remand in prison long enough.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: He has been given a Serious Crime Prevention Order which will last five years.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: It restricts his activity online including barring him from using Telegram and Discord.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: City of London Police said the case "highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online".
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: He hacked Rockstar games, Revolut and Uber while on bail and under police protection in a Travelodge in Bicester.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: He was there for protection from rival hackers who had threatened to attack him for his stolen stashes of Bitcoin.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: With his computer confiscated, Kurtaj hacked Rockstar using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into his hotel room television along with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: He stole internal company data including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished GTA 6, which had been shrouded in secrecy until its release last week.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: Rockstar Games said it cost the firm $5m (£3.8m) to recover from the hack, plus thousands of hours of staff time.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: The company also said the breach revealed for the first time that one of the playable characters in the game was a woman - a secret it was guarding closely for marketing purposes.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: When he was sentenced he stood and smiled.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: He had short hair and an unkempt beard and wore a suit and buttoned-up white shirt without a tie.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: The hacker blinked frequently during the hearing.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: The Judge Mr Justice Turner told him "you are a very talented young man," and warned him: "Don't let this happen again." Kurtaj's defence team said he found the online world a more comfortable way of interacting with other people.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: "The restricted and repetitive patterns of behaviour and interests that are a core feature of ASD [autism spectrum disorder] led him to become preoccupied with the online world where he felt better able to function and exist," they said.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: They said he was exposed to people who showed him how to cheat at games and then to "people who were involved in hacking".
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: During the pandemic, he was "very isolated" and his "connection to Lapsus$ provided him with a sense of community and self-worth that had been absent in his life previously," they added.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: Previously, the court heard that during his hack on Uber he posted a picture of a penis as part of his attempts to force the company to pay a ransom.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: His hacks on the companies are estimated to have caused around £10m of damage.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: Using the data stolen from the firms, he and other members of the gang targeted cryptocurrency investors.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'

sentences.text: The 26-year-old content creator had the world at her feet when she went viral in 2023 , going on to build a social media following of more than 900,000 people.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: She signed major brand endorsement deals and was pursuing a music career.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: Her symptoms made her violent and erratic, leading to her being sectioned in a mental health hospital - where doctors treated her with anti-psychotic medication.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: But Bahsoon's family, helped by her father's neurologist friend, pushed for further tests.

sentences.text: And two months into her hospital treatment, doctors got to the truth.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: Sabrina Bahsoon shot to fame for her viral Tube videos but in March 2026 her life turned upside down overnight.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: She actually had a rare, but treatable, autoimmune disease which is known to sometimes present as psychiatric symptoms, as well as seizures, confusion and memory loss.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: In her first interview since the experience, she tells BBC News she wants hospitals to offer a series of tests as standard practice if patients have these symptoms.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: "In a way I do feel let down by the care I received.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: I feel like the urgency to discover what was actually wrong with me wasn't there," she says.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: "And I also feel as a woman being written off completely as a psychotic patient without further investigation was a mistake." A spokesperson for the hospital she attended has apologised for Bahsoon's experience and says an investigation has been launched into her care.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: The content creator was in hospital for about four months earlier this year Bahsoon first had "psychotic symptoms" in March this year after filming a video on the Tube with girl group Flo.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: She says that evening she began to scream, cry and her conversations became "very erratic".
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: The next day she broke up with her boyfriend, which prompted her sisters to check on her, as it was so unexpected.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: Bahsoon says her condition got worse, becoming violent towards herself and posting videos which didn't make sense, before her sisters called 999 for an ambulance.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: "I'm normally a very relaxed person, maybe anxious at times, but the way I was speaking about harming myself and the way I was screaming and being violent was super out of character for me," she says.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: A&E doctors initially thought her symptoms could have been provoked by stress and a lack of sleep, discharging her with sleeping tablets.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: She then began destroying things at home and spoke about having hallucinations, which led to police bringing her to hospital in handcuffs.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: Bahsoon was sectioned and moved to a psychiatric ward where she was treated with antipsychotic medication, which she says made her "docile".
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: "I went from being a total firecracker to being completely catatonic," she says.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: "I stopped eating, drinking.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: I could not speak properly." Bahsoon has "very faint memories" of this period, she says, but her family has since shown her clips of her having breakdowns which she finds "heartbreaking".

sentences.text: Sabrina Bahsoon was pursuing a music career at the height of her fame After two months on the psychiatric ward, Bahsoon was diagnosed with an autoimmune disease called anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: It was caused by tumours in her ovaries, known as teratomas, producing antibodies which attacked her body.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: She had surgery to remove the tumours in June, which she says brought on a "drastic" change in her behaviour from "freaking out" to having more understanding of what was happening around her.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: Bahsoon has since been recovering back in her home country of Malaysia and is having therapy to "deal with all the trauma".
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: But she says she feels "very lucky" as doctors have told her she is part of a small percentage of people who they expect to make a full recovery.

sentences.text: She also wants to "push people to advocate for themselves" if they feel they're not getting the "treatment they deserve".
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: "I do want reform in the way that hospitals deal with psychotic patients or patients that present with psychotic symptoms," she says.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: "I hope I'm sharing my story so that nobody else has to go through this." She plans to return to her content creation in the new year and is looking forward to "enjoying life with a whole new perspective and appreciation for what I do and what I now can help people with".

sentences.text: I Am Helen charts a relationship spiralling after a non-consensual sexual experience This article contains spoilers for I Am Helen, and contains details some readers may find upsetting.

sentences.text: If you want to unwind on the sofa after a long day, I Am Helen probably isn't the show for you.

sentences.text: The Channel 4 drama starring Bridgerton star Nicola Coughlan and Joe Cole from Peaky Blinders has been called a must-watch by critics - but the cast don't want viewers sitting comfortably.

sentences.text: "There's going to be a few awkward sofas," Cole, who plays Helen's partner Steve, says.
sentences.article_title: Why Nicola Coughlan's new drama might leave viewers uncomfortable

sentences.text: "There's going to be people up and down the country that will be able to relate to this in varying degrees.

sentences.text: "And if we can put that in their living rooms and open up a debate, open up a conversation - and maybe help people be better - then we've done our job." I Am Helen is the latest project in writer and director Dominic Savage's I Am... series, female-led stories focusing on themes like mental health and relationships.
sentences.article_title: Why Nicola Coughlan's new drama might leave viewers uncomfortable

sentences.text: The two fully-improvised episodes, devised in collaboration with Coughlan, follow a relationship spiralling after Steve tries to choke Helen during sex without consent.
sentences.article_title: Why Nicola Coughlan's new drama might leave viewers uncomfortable

sentences.text: "We never realised how incredibly timely it would be," Coughlan tells BBC Newsbeat.
sentences.article_title: Why Nicola Coughlan's new drama might leave viewers uncomfortable

sentences.text: "We filmed this over a year ago.
sentences.article_title: Why Nicola Coughlan's new drama might leave viewers uncomfortable

sentences.text: "It feels incredibly relevant right now, and specifically right now, because pornography that includes strangulation has just been outlawed in the UK." Earlier this month, the government made it illegal for anyone to possess or publish porn that shows strangulation or suffocation.
sentences.article_title: Why Nicola Coughlan's new drama might leave viewers uncomfortable

sentences.text: That decision followed a review last year that found choking was "rife" on porn sites and had become normalised, particularly among younger people.
sentences.article_title: Why Nicola Coughlan's new drama might leave viewers uncomfortable

sentences.article_title: Why Nicola Coughlan's new drama might leave viewers uncomfortable

sentences.article_title: Why Nicola Coughlan's new drama might leave viewers uncomfortable

sentences.text: The Games Rating Authority administers PEGI age ratings on physical games in Europe Video games experience a similar process to films shown in UK cinemas, where examiners from the British Board of Film Classification watch each film before deciding its rating.

sentences.text: But rating games presents a unique challenge.

sentences.text: Modern games can contain huge worlds that take months to explore.

sentences.text: Some allow players to make their own choices, meaning two people can have vastly different experiences.

sentences.text: Developers first complete a GRA questionnaire disclosing any contentious content and provide at least two hours of footage, along with transcripts of the game's dialogue.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Examiners study this material, logging timestamps for instances of blood, gore, horror, drug use or bad language.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Examiner Sadie West is a fan of role-playing video games Lifelong gamer Sadie West joined the GRA believing it would be the dream job: being paid to play games.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: She says: "I definitely look at it more analytically when I'm playing here.
